title: Normal female karyotype
clinical_history: Demonstration metaphase prepared for laboratory teaching. The recorded sex is female. No clinical abnormality is provided.
plain_language_interpretation: A normal female diploid karyotype: 46 chromosomes with two X chromosomes and no reported numerical or structural abnormality.
diagnosis: No cytogenetic abnormality identified (normal female karyotype)
diagnosis_options: No cytogenetic abnormality identified (normal female karyotype)
No cytogenetic abnormality identified (normal male karyotype)
explanation: A standard female karyotype is 46,XX. Two X chromosomes occupy C-group positions. There is no Y chromosome in group G. Write the chromosome count first, then the sex-chromosome complement, with no further tokens when the study is normal.
hints: A normal female cell has 46 chromosomes and two X chromosomes; there should be no Y.
X chromosomes are medium-sized submetacentric chromosomes and are placed with group C (pairs 6–12).
If a small acrocentric chromosome is left after pairs 21 and 22 are filled, re-examine group G rather than assuming a Y is present.
